solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Girl with authoritarian ward

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, as in Princess Di
an authoritarian is strict about rules

explanation.surface: A young woman paired with a domineering guardian of a ward in care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ward' reads as a child in someone's care, but it is the administrative area of a town.
explanation.definitionFit: A ward is an electoral or administrative division of a city, which is a kind of district.

clue.text: Hold back beginning of precipitation and moisture

parts.note: to dam is to hold back water

indicators.note: 'beginning of' keeps only the first letter of 'precipitation'

explanation.surface: Blocking the start of the rain and its wetness.
explanation.definitionFit: Damp as a noun means slight wetness, a synonym for moisture.

clue.text: Attachment for motorcycle is raced all over the place

indicators.note: something all over the place is scattered in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A motorbike accessory is driven fast everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a one-wheeled passenger car fixed to the side of a motorcycle.

clue.text: Movement in arts mimics no art that is contrived

indicators.note: contrived means artificially put together, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: An artistic school that imitates without any real art is artificial.
explanation.definitionFit: Romanticism was the late 18th and 19th century movement in literature, music and painting.

clue.text: Opera about a king with followers

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, king
a leader's followers are his men

explanation.surface: An opera whose plot concerns a monarch and his retinue.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmen is Bizet's famous opera, so an example of the definition.

clue.text: Primarily two roping in one?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of each following word is kept

parts.note: the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A pair of people pulling a third into their group.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: two people roping in one more makes three.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair that takes on one extra member becomes a group of three, which is a trio.

clue.text: Jewish scholar's talk, never-ending

indicators.note: never-ending means without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to rabbit is to chatter, from rhyming slang rabbit and pork for talk

explanation.surface: A learned rabbi's lecture seems to go on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit on is British slang for talking at length.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a teacher and scholar of Jewish law.

clue.text: Gold supported by Kuwaiti currency and yen standard

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for yen

explanation.surface: Gold backed by Middle Eastern and Japanese money sets a monetary standard.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supported by' puts the first piece on top of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary and standard both describe something normal and unremarkable.

clue.text: Precocious little girl's angry morning

parts.note: a.m. is the abbreviation for morning

explanation.surface: A child prodigy wakes up in a foul temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a madam is a cheeky, precocious or bossy young girl.

clue.text: Potential flower our beds might produce?

indicators.note: the letters of the words produce something new once rearranged, which is what might produce hints at

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders what bloom their flowerbeds will grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A bud is an unopened flower, so a rosebud is a rose still to come.

clue.text: Say actor's words with Shakespeare's capital majesty

parts.note: the capital, or first letter, of Shakespeare

explanation.surface: Delivering a Shakespearean actor's speech with regal grandeur.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty in the sense of impressive dignity is stateliness.

clue.text: Near ancient? That could be it

definitions.text: Near ancient? That could be it

indicators.note: could be suggests the preceding words may become something else once their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone asks what might be described as almost ancient.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words are both the anagram letters and, read normally, a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has reached a hundred years of age is getting close to being ancient.

clue.text: Book is difficult to endorse

explanation.surface: A volume that is hard to recommend.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardback is a book bound in stiff covers.

clue.text: Scared of a loud attack

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: Someone frightened of a noisy assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Afraid and scared are plain synonyms for feeling fear.

clue.text: Joker's taunt about solver's initial time

indicators.note: about means around, so the taunt word goes round the other letters

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The setter Joker teases the solver by mocking how long they took.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter of this puzzle is called Joker, so the clue looks like a self-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: A jester was a court fool whose role was to make jokes, so a joker.

clue.text: Tons to wrap more than nine times

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: Heavy loads to be packaged repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenfold means ten times as much, which is one step beyond nine times.

clue.text: Young girl needs help surrounded by males

indicators.note: surrounded by means enclosed, so the help word sits inside the males word

explanation.surface: A girl surrounded by men needs assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden is an old-fashioned word for a girl or young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Journey's end in entering key European terminus perhaps

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so the small word is placed within the terminus word

parts.note: a terminus is an example of a railway station

explanation.surface: A traveller's journey ends at a major European railway terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: The place where a journey finishes is its destination.

clue.text: Second shopping centre is limited in size

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A second retail complex turns out to be compact.
explanation.definitionFit: Small means of little size, so restricted in dimension.

clue.text: Closely watched every heartless editor

indicators.note: heartless means with the middle removed, so only the outside letters remain

parts.note: ed is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Each unfeeling editor was kept under scrutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it closely, so eyed means observed carefully.

clue.text: Capone carrying weapons caused consternation

parts.note: Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: The gangster Al Capone with guns upset everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' looks like a container signal, but here it just forms the phrase meaning armed.
explanation.definitionFit: To alarm someone is to cause them sudden fear or consternation; the past tense matches.

clue.text: English lad going around northern wood

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: going around means encircling, so the lad word is wrapped round the next letter

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: An English youth wanders around a forest in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a dense black hardwood from tropical trees.

clue.text: A thousand I will murder

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, as in kilo
I'll is the contraction of I will

explanation.surface: A hitman vows to commit a thousand murders.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill and to murder are both verbs for taking a life.

clue.text: Biased? Indeed so, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters end up in disorder

explanation.surface: Someone sadly admits to being prejudiced.
explanation.definitionFit: A biased view favours only one party in a dispute, so it is partial or one-sided.
